# zone_mail_account (Resource)

A mailbox on a webhosting service.

!> **Destroying this deletes the mailbox and the mail in it.**

~> **`address` does not force replacement, deliberately.** The address is the mailbox's identifier in the API, so renaming one is either an in-place move or a refusal. Marking it for replacement would mean a single-character typo destroyed a mailbox and its mail; as it is, a rename the API will not do fails the apply and nothing is lost.

~> **Secrets here are write-only arguments and need Terraform 1.11 or newer.** They are sent to zone.eu and never written to state, because state is not an encrypted store: a secret in it is a secret in every backup and CI artefact the state file passes through. The API agrees — it accepts these fields and never returns them.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A mailbox. The password is write-only: it is sent to zone.eu and never
# written to state, so Terraform cannot detect a change made in webmail.
resource "zone_mail_account" "info" {
  service_name = "virt1.example.com"
  address      = "info@example.com"

  password         = var.mailbox_password
  password_version = 1

  comment   = "Reception"
  spamlevel = "medium"
}

# Rotating the password means changing password_version as well, because
# Terraform cannot see a change to a value it does not keep.
variable "mailbox_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `address` (String) The mailbox address, for example `info@example.com`. The domain must be one the service serves.
- `service_name` (String) The webhosting service this belongs to. This is a virtual server name, which often looks like a domain but is a different namespace from a DNS zone — use the `zone_vservers` data source to list the valid values. Changing it moves the resource to another service, which means replacing it.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `comment` (String) A note on the mailbox, shown in the ZoneID panel.
- `forward_addresses` (Set of String) Addresses that a copy of incoming mail is also sent to. The mailbox still keeps its own copy; for forwarding without storage use `zone_mail_forwarder`.
- `password` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) The mailbox password.

Write-only: sent to zone.eu and never stored in state. Between 10 and 64 characters.
- `password_version` (Number) Change this to re-send `password`. Terraform cannot see a change to a write-only value, so rotating the password means changing this number as well — any new value will do. A password changed outside Terraform is undetectable by definition.
- `spamlevel` (String) How aggressively to filter spam: `none`, `low`, `medium` or `high`.
- `two_factor_auth` (Boolean) Whether two-factor authentication is on for this mailbox.

The API can only turn this **off**; the mailbox's owner turns it on in webmail. So `false` means "turn it off if the owner enabled it", and `true` is rejected during validation rather than by the API after an apply has started. Leave it unset to let the owner decide.

### Read-Only

- `autoreply` (Boolean) Whether an autoreply is active. Read-only here: the autoreply itself is a `zone_mail_autoreply` resource.
- `disabled_features` (Set of String) Features zone.eu has disabled for this mailbox.
- `disk_size` (Number) The mailbox quota in bytes.
- `disk_usage` (Number) Bytes currently stored.
- `resource_url` (String) API URL of this mailbox.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Mailboxes are imported as "<service name>/<address>". The password is not
# imported, because no state ever holds one; the next apply sends whatever the
# configuration supplies.
terraform import zone_mail_account.info "virt1.example.com/info@example.com"
```
